glosses: To get away from by cunning; to avoid by using dexterity, subterfuge, address, or ingenuity; to cleverly escape from.

examples.text: He evaded his opponent's blows.
The robbers evaded the police.
to evade the force of an argument
The heathen had a method, more truly their own, of evading the Christian miracles.

“Evading” is moving through ground occupied by an opponent without trying to knock him down. You can attempt this as part of any maneuver that allows movement, provided you can move fast enough to go past your foe – not just up to him.

If someone tries to evade you from the front (see Evading, p. B368) and you have a melee weapon that can parry, you may roll against weapon skill instead of DX in the Contest. You keep him from evading if you win or tie

glosses: To escape; to slip away; — sometimes with from.

examples.text: Evading from perils.

glosses: To attempt to escape; to practice artifice or sophistry, for the purpose of eluding.

examples.text: The ministers of God are not to evade and take refuge any of these ... ways.

glosses: To get free; to free oneself.

examples.text: The prisoners escaped by jumping over a wall.

glosses: To avoid (any unpleasant person or thing); to elude, get away from.

examples.text: The children climbed out of the window to escape the fire.
He only got a fine and so escaped going to jail.
sailors that escaped the wreck

glosses: To avoid capture; to get away with something, avoid punishment.

examples.text: Luckily, I escaped with only a fine.

glosses: To elude the observation or notice of; to not be seen or remembered by.

examples.text: The name of the hotel escapes me at present.
The detective examined the crime scene, but one clue escaped his notice.
